statement.p: The figure below gives a sketch of a velocity vector field \vec F = (-x-y)\vec i + (-x)\vec j in the xy-plane. Note that vectors are given with a dot at the tail of each arrow.

description.p: A vector field that points to the right and up on the positive x axis, to the right and up on the positive y axis, to the left and down on the negative x axis, and to the left and down on negative y axis.

statement.p: (a) What is the direction of rotation of a thin twig placed at the origin along the x-axis?
(b) What is the direction of rotation of a thin twig placed at the origin along the y-axis?
(c) If we put a paddle wheel at the origin, instead of a twig, in what direction would you expect that to rotate?

static.solution:
(a) A thin twig at the origin along the x-axis would only feel the velocity perpendicular to that axis, and thus would rotate in a clockwise direction.
(b) Similarly, if oriented along the y-axis, rotate in a counterclockwise direction.
(c) Combining (a) and (b), we expect the paddle wheel will not rotate.
(d) Using the Cartesian coordinate definition, we get \mbox{curl} \vec F=\left |\begin{array}{ccc}\vec i\amp \vec j\amp \vec k\\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\amp \frac{\partial}{\partial y}\amp \frac{\partial}{\partial z}\\ (-x-y) \amp (-x) \amp 0\end{array}\right | = \boldsymbol{0}. This is as expected, since a paddle-wheel (instead of a twig) placed in the field would behave as indicated in (c).
